title: Perimeter, area and volume
description: Animated KS3 Maths lesson on perimeter, area and volume for ages 9 to 14: perimeter of rectangles and compound shapes, area of rectangles, triangles, parallelograms and trapeziums, circumference and area of a circle, volume and surface area of cuboids, and area and volume units.
intro: How far round, how much surface and how much space inside, explained by the owl in five short parts.

steps.say: **Perimeter** is the distance all the way round the edge of a shape. Watch the owl walk round this rectangle.
The rectangle is 7 cm long and 4 cm wide. Add all four sides: 7 + 4 + 7 + 4 = **22 cm**. Perimeter is a length, so it is in cm.
steps.speak: The rectangle is 7 centimetres long and 4 centimetres wide. Add all four sides: 7 plus 4 plus 7 plus 4 is 22 centimetres. Perimeter is a length, so it is in centimetres.

steps.say: For an L shape, find the missing sides first. The top is 9 − 4 = 5 cm. The right side is 7 − 3 = 4 cm.
steps.speak: For an L shape, find the missing sides first. The top is 9 minus 4, which is 5 centimetres. The right side is 7 minus 3, which is 4 centimetres.

steps.say: Then add all six sides: 9 + 4 + 4 + 3 + 5 + 7 = **32 cm**.
steps.speak: Then add all six sides: 9 plus 4 plus 4 plus 3 plus 5 plus 7 is 32 centimetres.

check.q: A square has sides of 6 cm. What is its perimeter?
check.hint: A square has 4 equal sides. Add them all up.
check.explain: 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 4 × 6 = **24 cm**. (36 would be the area, in cm².)

steps.say: **Area** is how much flat surface a shape covers. We measure it in squares. A square 1 cm by 1 cm has an area of **1 cm²** (one square centimetre).
steps.speak: Area is how much flat surface a shape covers. We measure it in squares. A square 1 centimetre by 1 centimetre has an area of 1 square centimetre.

steps.say: This rectangle is 7 cm long and 4 cm wide. It has 4 rows of 7 squares. Area = length × width = 7 × 4 = **28 cm²**.
steps.speak: This rectangle is 7 centimetres long and 4 centimetres wide. It has 4 rows of 7 squares. Area equals length times width: 7 times 4 is 28 square centimetres.

steps.say: Don't mix them up! The same rectangle has a perimeter of 22 cm but an area of 28 cm². Area is always in **square** units.
steps.speak: Don't mix them up! The same rectangle has a perimeter of 22 centimetres but an area of 28 square centimetres. Area is always in square units.

steps.say: For the L shape, take the whole rectangle, 9 × 7 = 63 cm², and subtract the missing corner, 4 × 3 = 12 cm². Area = 63 − 12 = **51 cm²**.
steps.speak: For the L shape, take the whole rectangle, 9 times 7, which is 63 square centimetres, and subtract the missing corner, 4 times 3, which is 12 square centimetres. The area is 63 minus 12, which is 51 square centimetres.

check.q: A rectangle is 9 cm long and 3 cm wide. What is its area?
check.hint: Area of a rectangle = length × width. And area is in square units.
check.explain: 9 × 3 = **27 cm²**. (24 cm is its perimeter, and area is in cm², not cm.)

steps.say: A triangle is half of a rectangle. This one has a base of 8 cm and a height of 5 cm. Area = base × height ÷ 2 = 8 × 5 ÷ 2 = **20 cm²**.
steps.speak: A triangle is half of a rectangle. This one has a base of 8 centimetres and a height of 5 centimetres. Area equals base times height divided by 2: 8 times 5 divided by 2 is 20 square centimetres.

steps.say: The height must be **perpendicular** to the base: it meets the base at a right angle. It is not the slanted side.
A **parallelogram**: cut a triangle off one end and move it to the other end. Now it is a rectangle! Area = base × perpendicular height = 8 × 4 = **32 cm²**.
steps.speak: A parallelogram: cut a triangle off one end and move it to the other end. Now it is a rectangle! Area equals base times perpendicular height: 8 times 4 is 32 square centimetres.

steps.say: A **trapezium**: add the two parallel sides, halve the answer, then multiply by the height. (3 + 7) ÷ 2 = 5, and 5 × 4 = **20 cm²**.
steps.speak: A trapezium: add the two parallel sides, halve the answer, then multiply by the height. 3 plus 7 is 10, divided by 2 is 5, and 5 times 4 is 20 square centimetres.

check.q: A triangle has a base of 10 cm and a perpendicular height of 6 cm. What is its area?
check.hint: Area of a triangle = base × height ÷ 2. Don't forget to halve!
check.explain: 10 × 6 = 60, and 60 ÷ 2 = **30 cm²**. A triangle is half of a rectangle.

steps.say: The **radius** goes from the centre of a circle to the edge. The **diameter** goes all the way across, through the centre. The diameter is 2 × the radius.
steps.speak: The radius goes from the centre of a circle to the edge. The diameter goes all the way across, through the centre. The diameter is 2 times the radius.

steps.say: The **circumference** is the distance all the way round a circle. Unroll it and it is just over 3 diameters long: about 3.14 diameters. This number is called **π** (pi).
steps.speak: The circumference is the distance all the way round a circle. Unroll it and it is just over 3 diameters long: about 3.14 diameters. This number is called pi.

steps.say: So circumference = π × diameter. A circle with a diameter of 20 cm has a circumference of 3.14 × 20 = **62.8 cm**.
steps.speak: So circumference equals pi times diameter. A circle with a diameter of 20 centimetres has a circumference of 3.14 times 20, which is 62.8 centimetres.

steps.say: Area of a circle = π × radius × radius, written **πr²**. This circle has a radius of 10 cm, so its area is 3.14 × 10 × 10 = **314 cm²**.
steps.speak: Area of a circle equals pi times radius times radius, written pi r squared. This circle has a radius of 10 centimetres, so its area is 3.14 times 10 times 10, which is 314 square centimetres.

check.q: Use π = 3.14. What is the circumference of a circle with a diameter of 5 cm?
check.hint: Circumference = π × diameter. Here you already have the diameter.
check.explain: 3.14 × 5 = **15.7 cm**. (31.4 cm would be using 10 cm, double the diameter.)

steps.say: **Volume** is how much space a 3D shape takes up. We measure it in cubes. A cube 1 cm on each side has a volume of **1 cm³** (one cubic centimetre).
steps.speak: Volume is how much space a 3D shape takes up. We measure it in cubes. A cube 1 centimetre on each side has a volume of 1 cubic centimetre.

steps.say: This cuboid is 4 cm long, 3 cm wide and 2 cm tall. Each layer has 4 × 3 = 12 cubes, and there are 2 layers. Volume = length × width × height = 4 × 3 × 2 = **24 cm³**.
steps.speak: This cuboid is 4 centimetres long, 3 centimetres wide and 2 centimetres tall. Each layer has 4 times 3, which is 12 cubes, and there are 2 layers. Volume equals length times width times height: 4 times 3 times 2 is 24 cubic centimetres.

steps.say: **Surface area** is the total area of all the faces. A cuboid has 6 faces in 3 matching pairs: 4 × 3 = 12, 4 × 2 = 8 and 3 × 2 = 6. So the surface area is 2 × (12 + 8 + 6) = **52 cm²**.
steps.speak: Surface area is the total area of all the faces. A cuboid has 6 faces in 3 matching pairs: 4 times 3 is 12, 4 times 2 is 8 and 3 times 2 is 6. So the surface area is 2 times 12 plus 8 plus 6, which is 2 times 26, which is 52 square centimetres.

steps.say: Watch the units. 1 m = 100 cm, so 1 m² = 100 × 100 = **10,000 cm²**, not 100! And 1 litre = 1000 cm³. Use cm² for small things like a book and m² for big things like a football pitch.
steps.speak: Watch the units. 1 metre is 100 centimetres, so 1 square metre is 100 times 100, which is 10 thousand square centimetres, not 100! And 1 litre is 1000 cubic centimetres. Use square centimetres for small things like a book and square metres for big things like a football pitch.

check.q: What is the volume of a cube with sides of 3 cm?
check.hint: Volume = length × width × height, and in a cube they are all the same.
check.explain: 3 × 3 × 3 = **27 cm³**. (3 × 3 = 9 is the area of just one face, and 54 cm² is the surface area.)
